Brings the official French **flood vigilance** (Vigicrues) and the **height and flow of the
rivers** near your home into Gladys, from the public open data of Vigicrues and Hub'Eau. No
account, no key.

> **This is a complement, not a safety alert system.** Data can be late, missing or wrong, and
> the integration depends on your Gladys, your Internet access and two public services. In a
> flood, follow the official instructions (vigicrues.gouv.fr, the prefecture, your town hall,
> 112). This integration is not affiliated with the French government (Vigicrues, SCHAPI).

## What you get

- **One device per gauging station** you follow: water height in metres, flow in m³/h (or m³/s, as you choose) when
  the station measures one, the **flood vigilance** of its river section (green, yellow,
  orange, red) and the date of the last reading.
- A station that stops sending is shown as such ("No new reading since…"): an old value is
  never sent again as if it were fresh.
- For the stations Vigicrues forecasts, the **forecast** of the height (and of the flow when
  it is published): the peak expected and the value in 24 hours, central, low and high, with
  the time of the peak.
- Two **scene triggers**: "Flood vigilance raised" (yellow, orange or red) and "Flood
  vigilance lowered", filtered by station, section and colour.
- A **dashboard widget**: your stations, their height, its trend (rising, steady, falling) and
  the vigilance colour.
- A **"Find stations"** button that lists the stations around your house, in a commune or a
  department, with their river.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant **5.2.0** or later.
- Internet access from Gladys: the integration reads `hubeau.eaufrance.fr` and
  `www.vigicrues.gouv.fr`.
- For "around my house": the location of your house in Gladys (Settings, Houses). With several
  houses, choose yours in the **House** setting. The integration asks for it at installation (the "location" permission); it is only used to
  find the nearest stations, never stored nor logged.
- Mainland France for the vigilance. Hub'Eau also covers the overseas departments: their
  stations get heights and flows, without vigilance.

## Configuration

### Settings

| Setting                       | What it does                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Station codes                 | Codes separated by commas (`O200004001, B540001001`), or the addresses of the station pages of vigicrues.gouv.fr.                            |
| Communes (INSEE codes)        | Every station in service of these communes: `31555` for Toulouse, `75056` for Paris. The INSEE code is not the postcode.                     |
| House                         | The house whose location is used by "Around my house" and "Find stations". Empty: the first house of Gladys that has a location.             |
| Around my house               | Also follows the 3 nearest stations that send readings, within 5, 10 or 20 km of your house.                                                 |
| Refresh interval              | 15 (default), 20 or 30 minutes. The vigilance and the forecasts are read every 30 minutes.                                                   |
| Flow unit                     | **m³/h** (default): the unit Gladys shows everywhere. **m³/s**: the unit of Vigicrues, without a unit in Gladys (the feature name gives it). |
| Language of the feature names | Names of the features of new devices and language of their texts (colour, last reading). French by default.                                  |

At most 20 stations come from the configuration. Save, then open the **Discover** tab and
create the devices you want. A station whose device you created stays followed even if you
remove it from the settings: delete the device to stop.

### Finding your stations

The **Find stations** button of the configuration lists the stations in service, nearest
first, with their river, their distance and whether they sent a reading in the last hours.
Type, in the "Where" field:

- nothing: the stations around the house chosen in the settings (10 km, or the chosen distance);
- an INSEE commune code: `31555`;
- a department and a name: `31 Toulouse`, `75 Seine`, `08 Meuse`;
- a station code: `O200004001`.

Copy the codes you want into **Station codes**, then save. The code of a station is also the
end of its page address on vigicrues.gouv.fr.

## Devices

One device per station, named like Hub'Eau names it ("La Meuse à Charleville-Mézières").
Its features are read-only:

| Feature          | Type (Gladys)       | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Water height     | Liquid depth, in m  | Height at the gauge, above its zero: a negative value is normal at low water. Not an altitude.                                                                                                           |
| Flow             | Water flow, in m³/h | Converted from the m³/s of Vigicrues (1 m³/s = 3,600 m³/h). With the **m³/s** unit, the feature is named "Flow (m³/s)" and has no unit: Gladys has none for m³/s. Only when the station measures a flow. |
| Flood vigilance  | Risk level          | The colour of the section of the station, as the Gladys risk badge: 0 green, 1 yellow, 2 orange, 3 red. Only for a Vigicrues station.                                                                    |
| Vigilance colour | Text                | Green, Yellow, Orange or Red.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Last reading     | Text                | Date of the last reading ("29/09 15:30"), or "No new reading since…" after 3 hours without one.                                                                                                          |

The height and the flow are only sent when they change, and once every 12 hours otherwise.
After 3 hours without a new reading they are no longer sent, so Gladys shows their real age.
A station that measures a flow later on gets the feature: the Discover tab then offers to
update the device.

**Changing the flow unit** changes the structure of the devices: the **Discover** tab offers
"Update" for each station that measures a flow. Until you do, the flow keeps being sent in the
unit of the created device, so the two are never mixed. A feature name is frozen when it is
created: rename it in the device ("Flow" or "Flow (m³/s)") if needed. The history already
recorded keeps its former unit.

### Forecasts

For the stations Vigicrues forecasts (mostly on the large rivers, such as the Loire at
Montjean-sur-Loire), the device gains forecast features, in the units of the readings:

| Feature                                        | Value                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Height: forecast peak (central), (low), (high) | The highest height expected over the horizon of the forecast (1 to 3 days), in the central scenario and at the low and high bounds of its range (80 % likely). |
| Height: time of the forecast peak              | When the central peak is expected ("17/10 13:00").                                                                                                             |
| Height in 24 h (central), (low), (high)        | The height expected in 24 hours, in the same three scenarios. Not sent when 24 hours is beyond the horizon.                                                    |
| Flow: forecast peak…, Flow in 24 h…            | The same for the flow, only when Vigicrues forecasts it too (rare), in m³/h or m³/s like the flow.                                                             |
| Forecast issued                                | Production date of the forecast, or "No current forecast" once its last point is past.                                                                         |

Each scenario has its own peak: the low and high peaks may come at another hour than the central
one. The forecasts are read every 30 minutes (Vigicrues issues them a few times a day), and a
value is sent only when it changes. The peak says how high the water goes within the horizon,
the value in 24 hours how fast it comes: a value in 48 hours would add three features per series
for a level that lies between the two most of the time.

**Existing devices**: the forecast features appear the first time Vigicrues sends a forecast for
the station; the **Discover** tab then offers "Update" for its device. The existing features
keep their identifiers and their history. Most stations have no forecast: their devices do not
change.

## Dashboard widget

Add the **Vigicrues** widget to a dashboard.

- Without setting: one line per station (10 at most) with its height and trend, coloured by
  the vigilance of its section: green, yellow, red for orange and red (the widget palette
  has no orange, the heading gives the exact colour). Grey: no section, or no recent reading.
- With a station chosen: its height and flow tiles (with the flow unit, m³/h or m³/s), live, then its vigilance with the name of
  the section, its trend and its last reading.

For a station Vigicrues forecasts, the detail ends with the forecast peak: central value,
range and time ("2.9 m (2.56/3.24) · 01/10 16:40").

The widget ends with the source and its date, and a link to Vigicrues.

## Scene triggers

**Flood vigilance raised**: the section of a followed station goes to yellow, orange or red,
or to a higher colour. **Flood vigilance lowered**: it goes back to a lower colour.

Filters (all optional): the **station**, the **section** code (shown in the device
parameters, `VIGICRUES_SECTION`, e.g. `LO18`) and the **new colour**. Without a station
filter, a scene runs once per followed station of the section.

Variables for the actions: `station_name`, `river`, `section`, `section_name`, `color`
(`green`, `yellow`, `orange`, `red`), `color_name` (in the language of the settings),
`previous_color`, `previous_color_name`.

The triggers fire only for the stations whose device exists, never at the first reading, and
not after more than a day without vigilance (a restart, Vigicrues unreachable). A height
threshold is a scene condition on the "Water height" feature, not a trigger.

A forecast threshold needs no trigger of the integration: use the native trigger "Device state
change" on "Height: forecast peak (high)" (or central, or low: as cautious as you want), with
the option that fires only when the threshold is crossed. The scene then runs once when the
forecast goes above the threshold, not at every new forecast. The threshold is in metres, or in
the unit of the device for a flow.

## Scene examples

- **Orange or red near home**: trigger "Flood vigilance raised", colour orange and red →
  send a message "Vigilance \{\{color_name\}\} on \{\{section_name\}\}: check vigicrues.gouv.fr" and
  turn a light red.
- **All clear**: trigger "Flood vigilance lowered", colour green → message "Back to green on
  \{\{section_name\}\}".
- **Height threshold**: trigger "Device state change" on "Water height" of your station,
  above 3.5 m → send a message to everyone at home.
- **High forecast above 4.5 m: move things out of the water's way**: trigger "Device state
  change" on "Height: forecast peak (high)" of your station, above 4.5 m, only when the
  threshold is crossed → send the message "The high forecast of Vigicrues goes above 4.5 m:
  check the time of the peak and vigicrues.gouv.fr". With the central peak instead, the alert
  comes later and less often.
- **Station silent**: none needed: the "Last reading" feature says it, shown on the dashboard.

## Data sources, licence and quotas

- **Vigicrues** (`www.vigicrues.gouv.fr/services`): the vigilance of every section
  (`InfoVigiCru.geojson`, about 2.2 MB, issued at least twice a day), read every 30 minutes,
  and the stations of each section (read once a week). © VIGICRUES.
- **Vigicrues forecasts** (`previsions.json`): for the stations that have one, hourly points
  with a central value and an 80 % range, read every 30 minutes. A station without forecast is
  asked again every 6 hours. © VIGICRUES.
- **Hub'Eau Hydrométrie** (`hubeau.eaufrance.fr/api/v2/hydrometrie`): the stations and their
  real-time readings, updated every 5 minutes from the national hydrometric platform, kept one
  month. One request per refresh for all your stations.
- Both are published under the **Licence Ouverte / Open Licence Etalab 2.0**: free reuse,
  citing the source and its date — the widget shows both.
- Neither service publishes a quota. The integration stays light: one Hub'Eau request per
  refresh (15 minutes at most), the vigilance every 30 minutes, the referential once a week,
  and it names itself in its requests. Hub'Eau may refuse abusive use: do not lower these
  delays.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Unknown station code"**: Hub'Eau does not know this code. Check it with "Find stations"
  or on vigicrues.gouv.fr (the end of the station page address).
- **No vigilance feature**: the station is not on a Vigicrues section (many small rivers are
  only measured), or Vigicrues did not answer when the device was published: the integration
  tries again every hour, then the Discover tab offers to update the device.
- **No forecast feature**: Vigicrues does not forecast this station (most stations), see its
  page on vigicrues.gouv.fr. If it does, use "Update" for the device in the Discover tab. A
  forecast of the height without one of the flow is normal: Vigicrues often forecasts the
  height only (Montjean-sur-Loire, for example).
- **No flow feature**: the station measures only the height (Charleville-Mézières, for
  instance).
- **"No new reading since…"**: the station stopped sending (maintenance, failure, flood
  damage). Hub'Eau keeps one month: after that, "No reading for over a month".
- **"Hub'Eau does not answer"** or **"Vigicrues does not answer"** in the configuration: the
  service is down or Gladys has no Internet access. The values come back by themselves.
- **"Around my house"** does nothing: give your house a location in Gladys (Settings,
  Houses); the configuration screen says so. If you chose a house in the **House** setting,
  its location is the one that counts: the configuration screen names it when it has no
  location or no longer exists (choose another one, or empty the field).
- **Logs**: quiet by default (start, a station silent or back, a vigilance change, failures
  once). `LOG_LEVEL=debug` shows each refresh.

## Limits

- **Not a safety alert system**: a complement only, without any guarantee of delay or
  availability. The official instructions prevail.
- The vigilance covers mainland France only; the overseas services of Vigicrues are not read.
- The heights are stages above the gauge zero of each station: they cannot be compared from
  one station to another, nor with an altitude.
- Real-time readings are raw, not validated: outliers happen.
- Some stations send once an hour, up to about 75 minutes late.
- The forecasts are those of Vigicrues, with their uncertainty: the level is expected within
  the range 8 times out of 10, not always. Vigicrues revises them a few times a day.
- Tested against real answers of Hub'Eau and Vigicrues recorded in September and October
  2026, not yet on a live Gladys: feedback welcome.
- Not affiliated with the French government (Vigicrues, SCHAPI) nor with Hub'Eau.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Vigicrues asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your stations | `section` | No | Follow the gauging stations of your rivers: by code, by commune, or the nearest ones to your house. "Find stations" below lists them with their river. Save, then create the devices in the Discover tab. |
| Sources and limits | `section` | No | Data © Vigicrues and Hub'Eau (Licence Ouverte Etalab 2.0), read without an account. A complement, not a safety alert system: the official instructions prevail. Not affiliated with Vigicrues. |
| Station codes | `string` | No | Codes separated by commas, or the addresses of their Vigicrues pages. |
| Communes (INSEE codes) | `string` | No | Every station in service of these communes, e.g. 31555 for Toulouse, 75056 for Paris. |
| House | `select` | No | The house whose location is used by "Around my house" and by "Find stations". Empty: the first house of Gladys that has a location. |
| Around my house | `select` | No | Also follow the 3 nearest stations that send readings, within this distance of the location of your house in Gladys. |
| Refresh interval | `select` | No | Stations send a reading every 5 to 60 minutes. The vigilance and the forecasts are read every 30 minutes. |
| Flow unit | `select` | No | m³/h: the unit Gladys shows on every screen. m³/s: the unit of Vigicrues, shown without a unit (the feature name says it). Changing it: "Update" the devices in the Discover tab. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Names given to the features of new devices (Water height, Flow…) and language of their texts (colour, last reading). |

## How to install Vigicrues in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Vigicrues appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-vigicrues:1.2.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-vigicrues](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-vigicrues).

Vigicrues requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Vigicrues is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
